A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSS research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original HH-RLHF experiments, including acceptance rates, reward and inference efficiency comparisons, draft-model ablations, and gamma sensitivity in Table 1 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains original HH-RLHF results in Section 4 and Appendix D and adds an empirical comparison against DPO- and PPO-trained target models in Table 6.

M1.justification: The draft alignment procedure, Algorithm 1, acceptance and residual distributions in Equations (6)-(7), and gamma modification in Equation (14) are unchanged. The new target-model comparison evaluates the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use HH-RLHF for helpfulness and harmlessness alignment. The added target-model comparison introduces no new dataset, domain, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains Vanilla, BoN, TreeBoN, CARDS, and Vanilla SD. V3 adds a separate comparison against DPO- and PPO-trained Llama-3-8B target checkpoints in Table 6.

E3.justification: The stated model pairs, draft-training hyperparameters, gold reward model, temperature of 0.8, and 128-token limit are unchanged. Table 6 adds comparators without describing a distinct evaluation metric or testing procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a diagnostic intended to examine proximity to the RLHF optimum through comparisons with aligned target checkpoints. The draft-training and gamma ablations move from C.3 to D.1-D.2 without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly describe Table 4 as a single-run comparison. V3 introduces no repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; Table 6 also reports point estimates only.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1, 4, and 5 and Figure 2 are unchanged. New Table 6 reports gold rewards of 4.85 for DPO, 5.62 for PPO, and 6.14 for SSS. The SSS value repeats Table 4 rather than showing an improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its assumptions, and Appendix B's derivations are unchanged. V3 labels an existing step in Equation (10) and explains its connection to Equation (6), without adding or correcting mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims of RLHF-optimal sampling, alignment without an external reward model during inference, and favorable alignment-efficiency tradeoffs. The new appendix comparison does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 newly attributes the trained targets' lower gold rewards to their being approximations to the RLHF optimum. The earlier mechanism discussion is relocated to Appendix C, while the limitations concerning draft alignment and generalization remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds an implementation link to the authors' CARDS repository and identifies the DPO/PPO checkpoint sources in Appendix D.3. Existing training and hardware details are retained. The reproducibility statement still promises public code upon acceptance, so the added pointer does not establish actual availability.

R1.justification: V3 removes the DistillSpec citation by Zhou et al. from Appendix A.2 and the bibliography. Software references are formalized and several publication records updated, while the substantive positioning relative to alignment and speculative decoding research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V1's brief Section 4 points readers to Appendix C. V3 brings experimental settings and main results into Sections 4.1-4.2 and separates the existing explanation and ablations into Appendices C and D. This substantially reorganizes the empirical narrative despite largely retaining its wording.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 6, relocates Tables 2-4 into the main text, redraws Figure 1 with cleaner axes and legend styling, and adjusts table spacing and captions. The unchanged Figure 3 moves to a separate page; existing display content is otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Moving settings and main results into Section 4 makes the empirical case easier to assess, while the aligned-target comparison and source pointers add useful context. These gains are limited: the existing evidence and single-run reporting remain unchanged, and Table 6's gold rewards alone do not establish recovery of the KL-constrained optimum or explain the baseline gaps.
